title: Region assurance & KMS segregation - Auriga Learning
summary: High-level security and residency review focused on ensuring EU-only processing for student data, KMS key custody options, and subprocessor mapping. Redwood walked through routing and failover controls; customer requested SOC 2 evidence, DPA edits, and an on-prem-like private routing POC for EU-bound traffic.
topics: KMS key custody and split-escrow options
RBAC / SSO mapping with SAML + SCIM
action_items: Jordan Patel: Share SOC 2 Type II report + redacted penetration test summary — due 2027-06-10
Maya Chen: Provide architecture diagram showing EU-only routing + fallback policy — due 2027-06-11
Liam O'Donnell: Send Auriga's minimal DPA redlines for review — due 2027-06-14
next_steps: Redwood to email SOC2 + security pack and link to subprocessor list
Customer to propose dates for an EU-only POC (3-week window)
Schedule legal follow-up to walk DPA redlines (Elena + Jordan)
SE to run a short routing demo showing region affinity and failure to fallback
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We can start, um, just to set context this is a security and residency review — we want to cover EU-only processing for student records, KMS and subprocessor questions, and the typical SOC2 and DPA items.
[00:18] Liam O'Donnell: Thanks Jordan. Quick intro, I'm Liam, CISO at Auriga, we run EU-based learning platform for 12 countries, data residency is non-negotiable for a subset of PII.
[00:30] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya here, head of Cloud Ops, we'll be owning integrations. We need details on routing, failover, and SSO.
[00:40] Elena Morales: Elena, legal — I'll focus on DPA and subprocessors.
[00:45] Jordan Patel: Great — Maya from our infra team will do the deep dive in a minute.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Hi team, thanks. Quick note: apologies if audio clips, we had a brief network blip earlier.
[01:05] Maya Chen: So first, region pinning: Redwood supports per-tenant routing rules. You can set processing affinity for EU regions, and we enforce at the edge. That means inbound requests from Auriga's tenants are routed to eu-west clusters.
[01:28] Priya Rao: And if eu-west is saturated or down, what's the fallback? Is there automatic cross-border failover?
[01:36] Maya Chen: Good question. By default we offer policy-based fallback — you can set strict no-cross-border, or allow failover to a compatible EU replica in another EU region. Cross-border to US is opt-in only and would require explicit config plus DPA amendment.
[01:55] Liam O'Donnell: We need strict no-cross-border for student PII — any exceptions to that?
[02:02] Jordan Patel: Not by default. We can do strict enforcement that prevents routing outside EU. However, for catastrophic failure scenarios we can discuss a manual emergency plan, but that requires pre-approval and legal sign-off.
[02:20] Elena Morales: We'll want that in the DPA — an annex for disaster recovery exceptions.
[02:27] Maya Chen: Noted. Next, KMS: Redwood supports customer-managed keys in two models: 1) KMS in customer cloud (bring-your-own-key) where the CMK is in your cloud KMS and Redwood only gets a wrapped key; 2) Split custody / escrow where we hold an operational key copy and you keep the master in escrow — third option is Redwood-managed with HSM-backed keys.
[02:52] Priya Rao: For Auriga we want full control — keys in our GCP KMS or AWS KMS. How is encryption handled for transient KV-cache and model artifacts?
[03:04] Maya Chen: All KVs and caches at rest are encrypted with volume keys; when you BYOK, the data encryption keys are wrapped by your CMK. Model shards in the serving layer are encrypted as well and access is gated by role-based keys. There's an audit trail for key unwrap operations.
[03:22] Liam O'Donnell: Is there proof of no-exfiltration? We need to see audit logs showing key usage with metadata.
[03:29] Maya Chen: Yes — we emit key-usage logs including principal, operation, timestamp, and request id. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export; retention configurable.
[03:40] Elena Morales: What about subprocessor list — we need a full inventory, and subprocessor contracts that include EU adequacy clauses.
[03:48] Jordan Patel: We'll share the current subprocessor inventory — it's in the security pack. We do require subprocessors to meet our security baseline, and for EU we ensure SCCs or equivalent safeguards are in place.
[04:00] Priya Rao: Any edge vendors or caching partners outside EU? That would be a red flag for us.
[04:06] Maya Chen: Most of our edge nodes for EU routing are inside EU regions; we do have some telemetry and monitoring providers that are global, but PII is not sent to them — only anonymized metrics. We'll highlight any vendor that has telemetry that could be sensitive.
[04:22] Liam O'Donnell: On SOC2/ISO, can you confirm latest dates? We need the latest SOC 2 Type II and the scope covering hosting and processing.
[04:32] Jordan Patel: Sure — our latest SOC2 Type II ended March 2027. We'll attach the report; it covers hosted API, core serving, and observability. For ISO we are currently in progress with ISO 27001 recertification — we'll include status.
[04:46] Elena Morales: Please redact client names in the report when you send.
[04:49] Jordan Patel: Absolutely.
[04:52] Priya Rao: RBAC and SSO — we use SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. How granular is Redwood's RBAC? Can we map roles to our internal OU?
[05:02] Maya Chen: Yes — we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC is resource-scoped: you can create roles scoped to tenant, environment, and route. We also have attribute-based access control hooks if you want group-level mapping.
[05:17] Liam O'Donnell: Retention on audit logs — we need 7 years for certain records per regs. Is that possible?
[05:24] Maya Chen: Long-term retention is configurable but is an add-on for large volumes. We can export logs to your cloud for indefinite retention; our default retention is 90 days for high-verbosity logs but we can arrange exports and archived storage.
[05:38] Elena Morales: About data subject access — do you have a workflow for deletions and data subject requests spanning backups and caches?
[05:46] Maya Chen: We have a deletion pipeline; live data is erased immediately upon request, caches are invalidated, and we mark data for scrub on next backup cycle. Backups are handled via encrypted snapshots and we can run targeted scrubs, but need to coordinate RPO windows.
[06:02] Priya Rao: For the POC we'd want to route production-like traffic to EU-only nodes and validate no egress. How fast can that be stood up?
[06:12] Jordan Patel: We can do a 3-week POC — two weeks for config and one week of validation, roughly. That includes audit log exports and a KMS proof of concept with your CMK.
[06:22] Liam O'Donnell: Any customers doing KMS BYOK and strict region pinning we can reference?
[06:27] Jordan Patel: We have references in regulated edutech and health; I'll provide anonymized case studies.
[06:32] Elena Morales: On DPA redlines — we'll send minimal redlines. One is to require that subprocessors are listed 30 days in advance and any subprocessor changes require approval for PII processing.
[06:43] Jordan Patel: We can accept a notice period and an approval mechanism for sensitive subprocessors — we'll put together language.
[06:50] Priya Rao: Technical deep-dive question: how do you prevent token leakage from KV cache? We use student tokens in prompts, so we need to ensure no persistence outside EU.
[07:01] Maya Chen: We scrub and tokenize sensitive fields by default when flagged. KV cache is per-tenant, encrypted, and never replicated outside the configured region in strict mode. We also have prefix caching rules so sensitive prompts aren't cached.
[07:20] Liam O'Donnell: Can you export the audit log format example so our SecOps can run ingestion tests?
[07:26] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll share a sample schema and a small test payload you can ingest.
[07:35] Jordan Patel: Quick pause — I'll recap action items near the end and then hand off to legal for DPA specifics.
[07:44] Elena Morales: Also want to confirm incident response SLAs andpoint of contact in eu timezone.
[07:51] Jordan Patel: We'll provide a local emergency contact and outline incident classification and SLA targets.
[08:00] Maya Chen: One more note on subprocessor flow: if a subprocessor is in scope for EU processing, we require contractual assurances and geofencing in our routing layer so that data paths don't cross.
[08:15] Priya Rao: Good. For the POC, we'd also like to run a controlled failover test to see that strict mode prevents any US egress even during simulated outage.
[08:26] Maya Chen: We can simulate regional outage in a staging cluster and show no cross-border egress under strict policy — that will be part of the demo.
[08:35] Liam O'Donnell: About the KMS escrow option, if we ever need Redwood's operational support to decrypt in emergency, how's authorization handled?
[08:44] Maya Chen: Escrow requires two-party approvals: your legal approves a request and an internal Redwood security council signs off; all operations are logged and you can require an on-chain or notarized approval if you want stronger non-repudiation.
[09:00] Elena Morales: We might propose a narrow emergency clause with strict governance.
[09:05] Jordan Patel: Makes sense. We'll draft a proposed annex.
[09:10] Priya Rao: Any performance implication of BYOK and envelope encryption?
[09:16] Maya Chen: Minimal — unwrap latency is negligible relative to model inference. We use per-session DEKs cached securely to avoid hitting KMS on every token.
[09:26] Liam O'Donnell: Are there any subprocessors outside EU that touch metadata which could be considered personal?
[09:34] Jordan Patel: Not intentionally — we segregate PII from telemetry. We'll annotate the inventory with exact data flows so you can review.
[09:44] Elena Morales: Regarding legal retention, we'll need confirmation that backups can be purged upon DSAR — that's a requirement.
[09:51] Maya Chen: We'll document the backup scrub process and expected timelines; some retention windows depend on storage provider snapshots but we'll provide SLA for purge actions where possible.
[10:08] Jordan Patel: Okay I'm going to summarize the follow ups: SOC2 and security pack, subprocessor inventory, architecture diagram for EU-only routing, sample audit logs and ingestion schema, and a proposed DPA annex for disaster recovery exceptions and subprocessor notices.
[10:28] Liam O'Donnell: That aligns.
[10:31] Elena Morales: One ask — include an exportable list of all vendors with data processing locations annotated.
[10:37] Jordan Patel: Noted.
[10:40] Priya Rao: We'll pick potential POC dates after reviewing docs.
[10:44] Jordan Patel: Great — thanks all, we'll follow up via email.
[62:30] [call ends]
